facility.name: La Petite Academy
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Accredited,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Skill Classes,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 5432 BASSWOOD BLVD, FORT WORTH, TX, 76137

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: This standard was evaluated in regard to a report and found deficient. A caregiver was observed yelling at children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Electrical Outlets Covered: At the time of inspection, several outlets did not have plug covers.  Photographs were taken.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Electrical Outlets Covered (26 TAC §746.3701(1))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: At the time of inspection , one caregiver had not checked in 6 children she was caring for.  The children had been at the operation for 30-60 minutes without having been checked in on the iPad.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: At the time of inspection, the fire drill log indicated the last drill occurred in May 2026.  A drill was completed at the time of inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Placement of Groups - Groups Kept Separate: One caregiver was observed supervising two separate room, the caregiver was sitting by the door that separate the rooms. The caregiver was supervising 22 children over the age of 18 months old.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Placement of Groups - Groups Kept Separate (26 TAC §746.1505(1))

occurrences.finding: Naptime Child/Caregiver Ratio - Groups Not Combined Not Reduced: The area used in central nap time location were observed with limit space between mats, furniture, and children mats were place in areas that might limited the view of all children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Naptime Child/Caregiver Ratio - Groups Not Combined Not Reduced (26 TAC §746.1613(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Provides Access to Walkway: The nap time room arrangement did not provide sufficient space for caregiver and children walk between mats without walking over other children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Provides Access to Walkway (26 TAC §746.2909(4))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Use Disposable Gloves: A caregiver was seen not initially using gloves during diaper changing a child.  The caregiver corrected the action and put gloves on to finish the diapering.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Use Disposable Gloves (26 TAC §746.3505(c))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: Caregiver tried to force a child to sleep. Force was used by grabbing the child's arm and pulling their leg forward to lay flat on a sleeping cot.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver grabbed a child's arm and pulled their leg forward during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Alternate Activity for Non-sleeping Children: A caregiver did not provide an alternative activity to a child who was not sleeping during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Alternate Activity for Non-sleeping Children (26 TAC §746.2907(a))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: Health statements missing in two children's files.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: Three personnel files were missing proof of education requirement.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985): Two personnel files were missing affidavits.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Physician Information: One children's file missing physician information.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Physician Information (26 TAC §746.605(10))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Monthly feeding instructions was not available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Personnel Record Storage - Training Records: Six personnel training records were not accessible at the time of inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personnel Record Storage - Training Records (26 TAC §746.907(b))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: Health statements missing in three children's files.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: At the time of inspection the loose-fill surfacing (mulch) on the playground was observed to be less than 2 inches under climbing equiipment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver used prohibited punishment by grabbing a child's arms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Documentation PEDIATRIAC CPR-1st aid original certificate on file at center or copy available if licensing requests: Two caregivers CPR/First Aid training certificates were missing from personnel files.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation PEDIATRIAC CPR-1st aid original certificate on file at center or copy available if licensing requests (26 TAC §746.1329(c)(2))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Caregivers did not demonstrate self-control when using raised tone of voices and yelling while children were in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation. A caregiver did not demonstrate patience with a child during naptime.  This is evidenced through the caregiver?s actions towards the child such as pointing her finger in the child?s face, patting the child roughly on the back, and aggressively placing the child on a nap mat.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children (26 TAC §746.1201(2))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation.  Caregiver tried to force a child to sleep. Force was used by roughly placing the child's head on the mat and repositioning the child's arms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Access to Personnel Records: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation.  The training records for a caregiver were not available during the visit to the operation by the DFPS investigator.  The training records were requested multiple times by the Investigator before they were received.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Access to Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.909)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation.  A refrigerator was not secure and allowed children under the age of two to open the refrigerator; as a result, a child got injured.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan - No Long Waiting Periods: Evidence shows that a school age caregiver required the children to sit down on the carpet for at least 10 minutes or longer before engaging with the children. The caregiver did not give the children an activity or specific instruction.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - No Long Waiting Periods (26 TAC §746.2205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: At the time of inspection, children in the school age classroom were observed watching "Jumanji". One child was observed taking a nap on one side of the room. A couple other children were observed laying down, but they were not asleep.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio for Field Trips - Areas Open to General Public: There was evidence found proving that the operation was out of ratio while on a field trip. There were two groups of children on the field trip. The ratios of the groups were 12:1 and 14:1. The youngest child on the field trip was 6 years old. The 14:1 group was over ratio by 2 children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio for Field Trips - Areas Open to General Public (26 TAC §746.1801(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on information obtained through investigation it was found that a child was left inside the classroom while the rest of the class had gone to the outdoor play area. The child was left inside for less than 5 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: It was found that a caregiver did not notify or report to administration or parents when a child was left inside the classroom during a transition. It was also found that multiple caregivers had concerns regarding child safety and did not report this appropriately to administration.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: This standard was evaluated based on a reported incident. Evidence shows that the caregiver's pediatric first aid training was expired at the time of incident.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: A child in care with diagnosed food allergies, did not have a food allergy emergency plan on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on information gathered from a DFPS investigation, it is determined that the operation did not report the allegations within 48 hours to Licensing. The director was informed of the allegations on 8/15/2022 and Licensing received the report on 8/18/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Praise and Encouragement: A caregiver was observed on video grabbing several children by one arm and forcibly moving them from one place to the other in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Praise and Encouragement (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(A))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: A caregiver was observed on video grabbing several children by one arm and forcibly moving them from one   place to the other in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Children in Control: This standard was evaluated in regards to a report and found deficient. The toddler classroom was observed on   video for over 30 minutes being out of control. Children were observed standing on shelves, running and throwing toys.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups: An infant bottles were not properly labeled with the infant name, as a result an infant was fed with another infant  milk, this caused an allergic reaction to the infant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups (26 TAC §746.2419(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not ensure an infant bottles were properly labeled, as a result an infant was fed with another infant  milk, this caused an allergic reaction to the infant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Ten children's records were evaluated. Two children did not have an updated shot record on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))
